about.title: Turlock Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription:
Turlock is a working city. Between the shops along W Main Street and Geer Road, the businesses on N Golden State Boulevard, and the homes off Lander Avenue, people here rely on tools, appliances, vehicles, and equipment every day. When something does not perform as promised — a space heater that ignites, a tire that separates at highway speed, a child's car seat that fails on impact — the harm can be serious and the cause is not always obvious at first.

California treats these cases differently than an ordinary negligence claim. Under strict product liability, you generally do not have to prove the company was careless. You have to show the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach the manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer who sold it.

LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Turlock residents with an independent attorney who handles product cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My car had a mechanical failure on Lander Avenue. Is that a product case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Turlock recorded 331 injury collisions in 2025, and while most involve driver error, some trace back to a component that failed — brakes, tires, airbags, or steering. If a defect contributed to your crash, the manufacturer or parts supplier may be liable under strict liability in addition to any driver at fault. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney has looked at it.

items.question: Do I still have a claim if I bought the product used or secondhand?
items.answer: Possibly. California's strict liability rules generally apply to products sold in the ordinary course of business, so the answer depends on who sold it and how. An attorney can review the specific facts and tell you whether the manufacturer or an earlier seller in the chain may still be responsible.
